title: Where are you from?
grammar: Verb be: questions with Where; be in for location; be from for origin
pair_game: Show a flag. Your partner says the country and the nationality. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: Where + be from / be in
rows: Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.
grammar_box.tip: be from = country or city you come from; be in = place you are now (hozir qayerdasan)

questions: Where are you from? What is your hometown like?
What country are you from? What is your nationality?
Where is your school? Is it near your home?
What is the most famous city in Uzbekistan? Why is it famous?
Are there any students from other countries in your school?
Where are your favorite singers or actors from?
What country do you want to visit one day? Why?
Is Tashkent a big city? What can people do there?
Where are you right now — at school or at home? Describe the place.
What do you love most about your hometown or city?
starters: My school is in … . Yes, it is. / No, it isn’t.
The most famous city is … . It’s famous for …
Yes, there are. They’re from … / No, there aren’t.
My favourite singer is … . He’s / She’s from …
samples: Where are you from? What is your hometown like?
**I’m from** Namangan. My hometown is small and green.
What is the most famous city in Uzbekistan? Why is it famous?
**Samarkand** is very famous. It’s famous for **the Registan**!
Is Tashkent a big city? What can people do there?
Yes, **Tashkent is** a big city. People can ride the **metro** and go to **Magic City**.

mini_talk.title: My hometown
plan: Say one thing you love about your city
mini_talk.model: Hello! My name is Laylo. **I’m from** Bukhara. **I’m** Uzbek. Bukhara **is in** Uzbekistan. It **is** a very old city. My school **is in** the city centre. It **is** near my home. My friend Ali **is from** Kazakhstan. I love the old streets and the tasty bread in my city!
